system.name: DEPT
system.one_liner: A communication-efficient pre-training framework that decouples token embeddings from the transformer body so models train on several data sources without a shared vocabulary.

content.variant_note: a 2x2 grid of one identical left-to-right training pipeline for the STANDARD baseline and the TRIM, GLOB and SPEC variants, with numbered steps and a legend inside the first panel
content.argues: DEPT's three variants (TRIM, GLOB, SPEC) keep the same pipeline as standard pre-training but decouple embeddings from the transformer body to different degrees.
content.subject: Corpora, tokenizers, tokenized datasets, workers and a server holding an embedding layer (EL) and a transformer body (TB), drawn four times with small differences.

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw design variants as a 2x2 grid of one identical pipeline, number the steps once and change only the parts that differ (merged versus separate datasets, crossed-out or coloured embeddings, an aggregation equation present or absent), with the legend inside one panel.
lessons.suits: families of training-pipeline variants (federated, distributed, multilingual) where a few components change from variant to variant.

evidence: (3) WORKERS train the model on their pre-tokenized data; (4) partial training results are collected; (5) results are aggregated
we propose partially or fully decoupling the embedding space from transformer bodies

summary: DEPT is a communication-efficient pre-training framework that decouples token embeddings from the transformer body so that models can train on several data sources without a shared vocabulary. Figure 2 draws the standard pipeline and the three DEPT variants (TRIM, GLOB, SPEC) as a 2x2 grid of the same left-to-right schematic: flag-and-document icons for text corpora go through a tokenizer to blue and green tokenized datasets, then to workers and a server holding an embedding layer (EL) and a transformer body (TB). Dark numbered circles 1 to 6 order the steps, and plus and equals signs show how bodies and embeddings are aggregated; the variants differ in tokenizers, in crossed-out or colour-specific embeddings and in whether the server aggregates EL at all. A legend sits in the first panel.
summary_zh: DEPT 把词嵌入与 Transformer 主体解耦，使多数据源预训练无需共享词表。图2用2×2网格对比标准流程与 TRIM、GLOB、SPEC 三个变体，圆圈数字 1–6 标出步骤，加号和等号表示聚合。
notes: Prior kinds kept (design-family first) and stage-pipeline added because the caption describes numbered pipeline steps. The X marks over the EL tiles in TRIM are not explained in the legend; their reading as trimmed vocabulary entries follows the abstract (embedding parameters reduced to what the source vocabulary needs). Counts of icons are approximate (flags and badges from the digest, tiles by eye). The schema has no marker kind for plus and equals signs, recorded as other.
